seoTitle: Design a Real Estate Facebook Ad in Canva
metaDescription: Design a real estate Facebook ad in Canva: template, property photos, a feature checklist, the aspect ratio Meta now recommends for Feed, and the Housing ad category you must select.
intro:
A listing ad on Facebook gets seen by people who are scrolling, not searching. It has a second or two to register, so the design has to lead with one strong photo and a handful of facts.

This guide builds a listing ad in Canva from a Facebook Ad template: property photos from Uploads, a short headline, a checklist of features and an address line. It then covers two things that trip up real estate advertisers after the design is done. Canva's Facebook Ad canvas is landscape, while Meta now recommends a taller 4:5 image for Feed. And any ad for a home sale or rental has to run under Meta's Housing special ad category, which removes several targeting options.

steps.heading: Start a Facebook Ad design and pick a layout
steps.body:
Choose Facebook Ad as the design type. Canva opens a blank landscape canvas (Canva lists its feed ad size as 1200 × 628 pixels, a 1.91:1 ratio) with a "Search Facebook Ad templates" box on the left.

Search for something close to your listing and scroll. Few results will be real estate specific, and that's fine. Look for a structure you can reuse: a big headline zone, a large photo slot and room for a few lines of supporting text.

If the ad will run mainly in Facebook Feed, decide now whether to stay landscape. Meta's placement guide recommends 4:5 for Feed images. Landscape 1.91:1 is still accepted, but a 4:5 image takes up more of the screen. For 4:5, start a custom-size design at 1440 × 1800 pixels, Meta's listed minimum for that ratio.

image.caption: The Facebook Ad template search panel beside a blank landscape canvas.

steps.heading: Swap in the property photos
steps.body:
Open Uploads and either upload new listing photos with Upload files or pick ones already in your library. Drag each onto a photo slot in the template and it drops into the frame.

In this build a large living-room shot fills the right side, with two smaller photos (the kitchen and a dining area) stacked beside it. That gives viewers more than one room without shrinking the lead image. Put your best-lit, widest shot in the main slot, since it carries the first impression.

image.caption: Listing photos placed from Uploads: one large lead image with two smaller room shots beside it.

steps.heading: Write the headline, feature checklist and address
steps.body:
Replace the placeholder headline with the offer, kept short enough to read mid-scroll. Here it reads "New Luxury Apartments Now Open for Booking".

Under it, a checklist does more than a paragraph. Short phrases next to check icons ("Spacious 2-bedroom", "Modern amenities", "Flexible payment plans", "Limited units available") can be read at a glance. Finish with the address or neighbourhood on its own line with a location pin, so it's clear where the property is.

steps.heading: Finish the layout with Elements and your branding
steps.body:
The Elements panel groups Canva's library into Shapes, Graphics, 3D, Animations, Photos, Frames, Grids, Videos and Audio, and has a search box for keywords. Searches like "location pin", "bed" or "checkmark" turn up icons for a feature list. A thin divider between headline and checklist, or a frame around a secondary photo, helps a reused template look like your own.

Then swap the template colors for your agency's and place the logo somewhere consistent, such as a corner, where it won't fight the lead photo. If you run several listings, keeping logo position and colors the same makes the ads read as a series.

image.caption: The Elements panel open beside the finished ad, with shape, graphic and frame categories to browse.

steps.heading: Download, then run it under the Housing category
steps.body:
Download the design as PNG or JPG and upload it when you build the ad in Meta Ads Manager.

When you create the campaign, open Special Ad Categories and choose the category that applies, then pick the countries the campaign will run in. Ads for home sales, rentals and similar housing opportunities fall under Housing. For advertisers in or reaching the US, and those reaching Canada and some European countries, that category limits or removes age, gender, postal code, exclusion, lookalike and saved audiences, and expands city or pin-drop radiuses. Meta says ads can be rejected when the right category isn't chosen.

For the next listing, duplicate the Canva design and swap the photos, headline and checklist instead of starting again.

troubleshooting.problem: The ad was rejected even though the design is fine
troubleshooting.cause: The campaign wasn't set to a Special Ad Category. Meta requires advertisers to declare it for housing ads and says ads may be rejected without it.
troubleshooting.fix: Edit or recreate the campaign, open Special Ad Categories, choose Housing and select the countries it will run in.

troubleshooting.problem: Age, gender and postal code targeting have disappeared
troubleshooting.cause: That's the Housing category working as intended. Meta limits these options, plus exclusions, lookalike and saved audiences, for housing ads in the US, Canada and some European countries.
troubleshooting.fix: Target by city or pin location instead. Meta expands the radius automatically, so write the ad to suit a broader audience.

troubleshooting.problem: The ad looks small in the Feed next to other posts
troubleshooting.cause: Canva's Facebook Ad canvas is 1.91:1 landscape, while Meta recommends 4:5 for Feed images.
troubleshooting.fix: Rebuild the layout on a 1440 × 1800 px custom-size design and upload that version for Feed placements.

faq.question: What size should a real estate Facebook ad be?
faq.answer: For Facebook Feed, Meta recommends 4:5, with a minimum of 1440 × 1800 pixels at that ratio. Canva's Facebook Ad design type is 1200 × 628 (1.91:1), which Meta accepts but doesn't recommend for Feed.

faq.question: Do real estate ads need a special category on Facebook?
faq.answer: Yes. Ads about housing opportunities run under Meta's Housing special ad category, which you select when creating the campaign in Ads Manager. It limits some targeting options to help prevent discrimination.

faq.question: Can I make several listing ads quickly?
faq.answer: Duplicate the finished Canva design and swap the photos, headline and checklist for each property. The layout, colors and logo position carry over.

faq.question: Can I animate the ad?
faq.answer: Yes. Select an element or the page and use Animate in the toolbar, then download as a video or GIF. Check the video's aspect ratio against the placement you plan to use.

verifiedNote: The template search, photo placement and Elements panel come from a recorded Canva walkthrough. Aspect ratios, minimum image sizes and the Housing special ad category rules were checked against Meta's Business Help Centre, and Canva's stated ad size against its Facebook ad maker page, in September 2026. That check replaced this guide's earlier claim that Canva's template is pre-sized to Meta's recommendation; Meta now recommends 4:5 for Feed.
